about: Shape by gradient descent (G1, 2026-11-07, phases 1 and 2). Sources, with the exact figures and their use; derived results of deck/tools/gd. Embedded only in dist/gd.html (as GDSRC), never in main.html. G3 (F65.6): the side arcs felt over the whole slide as you grip; the long-arc trials rerun (deck/tools/gd/longarcs.py, out/longarcs.json). G4 (Brock 17:18): each side valley placed on its finger's slide as you grip; the palm-on-hump tips past the grooves scored; symmetry a rule; trial 3 the result. G5 (2026-11-08): the thumb placed from its base (thumb_g5, trials_g5_thumb_from_base). G6 (2026-11-08): the hand drawn as a realistic render posed by the model (hand_render_g6), and every joint's resting angle on its own slide with its source (joints_at_rest_g6).

sts57.title: Mount, Whitmore & Stealey, Evaluation of Neutral Body Posture on Shuttle Mission STS-57 (SPACEHAB-1), NASA/TM-2003-104805 (2003)

figures.msis_nbp: MSIS NBP lists wrist 0 / 0, elbow 90, shoulder flexion 36
figures.quote: in a forward position with the fingers curled at the knuckles (crew 2, p. 8)
figures.finger_flexion_joint: not stated (one value per hand; the text: "with the fingers curled at the knuckles", crew 2)

sts57.used_for: The rest pose in orbit: wrist straight; the fingers' flexion (mean 41 deg, 21 to 60) checked against the cascade's knuckle-to-tip angle (45 to 54 deg). Skylab is the MSIS's original source (cited by the TM); the TM itself says no one crew member showed the MSIS posture.
sts57.checked_g6: 2026-11-08: Table 1 read again for per-joint data: wrist extension and ulnar bend, finger flexion (one row), forearm pronation and supination; no MCP / PIP / DIP split, no thumb, no spread

varghese.title: Varghese, Venugopal, Srinivasan & Geetha Hari Priya, A Study on the Normative Values of Finger Flexion Cascade in Power Grip Users and Non-power Grip Users, JCDR 14(5) (2020) YC01-YC07

ansur2.title: ANSUR II public data, men (n = 4,082)
ansur2.used_for: The reference hand (the deck's ruler, b07_size); middle finger from the palm crease = 193.3 - 116.5 = 76.8 mm scales the bone lengths. Phase 2: the 5th to 95th percentile hands (177 to 210 mm) give the spread of fingertip positions in each pocket's core; the breadth SD gives each fingertip's sideways spread (1.645 x 4.4 / 3 = 2.4 mm).

buryanov.title: Buryanov & Kotiuk, Proportions of Hand Segments, Int. J. Morphol. (2010), as tabulated in Design, Implementation and Control of an Underactuated Hand Exoskeleton (arXiv 2003.11598), table 'Average finger phalange sizes'

shi2020.title: Shi, Heung, Tang, Tong & Li, Verification of Finger Joint Stiffness Estimation Method With Soft Robotic Actuator, Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology 8 (2020) 592637
shi2020.used_for: The finger's own pull back to rest: k_tip = k / r^2 (derived). Flexion stiffness also stands in for side-to-side (abduction) stiffness at the knuckle: an assumption.

kuo2012.used_for: Range check; why the stiffness is passive (ligaments), present with no muscle effort.

milner1998.title: Milner & Franklin, Characterization of multijoint finger stiffness, IEEE TBME 45(11) (1998) 1363-1375

figures.relaxed: 20 % MVC gives 2 to 4 times the relaxed finger's maximum stiffness

milner1998.used_for: Context: a working finger is far stiffer than a relaxed one, so the relaxed value is the right one for a finger at rest.

figures.note: The abstract prints 'sides and button ... 0.6 % (0.35 N) and 0.8 % (0.43 N)'; the results text gives the sides as 0.43 (SD 0.13) N and Table 2's button column 0.35 (SD 0.06) N. This study uses the table and text. Office work, not gaming.

quotes: the sides do curve in, but essentially are straight at the middle
Neither the front nor back flare out much
The main buttons feature rather deep comfort grooves

tpu_ulx.used_for: The ULX's pockets: 2.5 mm per side in from the hump, 1.1 mm per side of front flare (derived from the widths), and its deep grooves.

brock_2026_11_08_thumb.title: Brock Liddicoat (designer's observation), 2026-11-08 07:21, asked whether to keep trial 3's waist at its rescored spot (z 23.7) or put it back where he liked it (z 14)
brock_2026_11_08_thumb.quote: actually no, the thumb never goes that far forward, that's unnatural

iss_body_measures.title: S. Rajulu, K. Young and H. Kim, Quantification of In-flight Physical Changes: Anthropometry and Neutral Body Posture (Body Measures), NASA (ISS), presentation, no year printed

figures.hand: qualitative only: in the relaxed phase hands at or below the NASA-STD-3000 posture (crouch), higher (stretch); no wrist, finger or thumb joint angles; analysis in progress

iss_body_measures.used_for: Checked for per-joint hand angles in orbit (G6): none. The orbit data stay STS-57's.

arc_fit.note: phase 1 reported 0.12 / 0.17 mm but stored the first, unbounded fit (0.133); regenerated in phase 2

strength.rule: kappa* = k_tip / N: the pocket pulls as hard as the finger does (drift and strain, each normalised, cost least at equal stiffness)

circle_check.applies_to: cores of about 30 mm: the palm-on-hump trials (heel_fwd thumb 31.1 mm); the palm-lifted cores are 10 to 14 mm (lifted_sym 31.8 mm, one pocket for two fingers)

derived.superseded: the phase-1 notch run (notch.py, descend.py): its rims made a second dip next to the Sora's own waist (Brock, 12:55: one minimum per finger)

slide_g3.decision: F65.6 (Brock ~14:20): the side arcs are felt over the whole distance the thumb slides as you grip ("Over the whole slide"), thumb and pinky
slide_g3.label: derived (hand model)
slide_g3.basis: As you take hold, the hand lands with the palm on the hump and the fingers relaxed (the heel placement: wrist back 15 deg, the relaxed cascade), then draws back and lifts into the zero-g grip with the fingertips on the buttons (the lifted placement, trial 4). The thumb (estimate: level with the index PIP) and the pinky (the little fingertip) stay on the sides, so each slides by the difference of its two placements. ANSUR II mean hand; 5th and 95th by scaling.
slide_g3.felt_rule: the waist arc turns at least 3.44 deg (Gordon & Morison 1982 mean + 2 SD) over the slide: kappa >= 0.060 rad / slide; R <= 351 mm thumb, 415 mm pinky
slide_g3.cover_rule: the waist arc's chord at least the slide plus the contact patch (9.1 mm at 0.43 N, Serhat 2022): 30.1 mm thumb, 34.0 mm pinky
slide_g3.no_direct_source: No published measurement of how far the thumb slides along a mouse side was found; searched mouse-use kinematics (thumb positions, data-glove angles) without a usable figure

cross_checks.clamp_in_place_mm: thumb 7.9 (6.4 to 9.6), pinky 2.9 (2.0 to 4.0): the hand already in trial 4 clamps down onto the hump with the tips held (slide_checks.py); a part of the motion
cross_checks.thumb_own_closure_mm: about 3.0: the tip relative to its metacarpal from rest (Lee & Jung) to a cylinder grasp (Buchholz & Armstrong 1992), phalanges from Freivalds; the slide is the hand's travel, not the thumb's own joints

slide_g3.previous: G2: felt over where the thumb lands, contact 9.1 + spread 1.1 = 10.1 mm: R 169 (trial 4 came out at R 155)
model_changes_g3: the sides felt over the slide (kappa* = 0.060 / slide); the grooves keep the landing rule
cover: the waist chord at least the slide plus the contact patch (thumb 30.1, pinky 34.0 mm; mirrored: the longer)
start: the Sora waist slid so its narrowest point (11.1 mm ahead of its chord middle) sits at the rest; the middle-at-rest start ran the thumb waist past the nose corner
mirrored pockets: each finger counted against its own rest (G2 counted both against the mean, hiding 10 mm off each)
the front arc at least 1 mm long (a negative length looped the outline)
the top outline within 2.5 mm of the Sora (estimate); unbound, trial 4 wandered 4.4 mm at the rear for no gain

path_g4.decision: Brock 17:18 (on the Trials slide): "trial 3 is by far my favorite the right 2 don't look right at all". Trial 3 (palm lifted, mirrored) becomes the result; symmetry a rule (a traditional mouse is mirror-symmetric); the scoring that made trial 3 the worst is fixed
path_g4.rule: each side valley's bottom on its finger's path as you grip (F65.6: felt over the whole slide), from where it lands (palm on the hump) to where it grips (palm lifted); no cost on the path, ((mm off the path) / 2)^2 off it, each finger against its own path (a mirrored valley counts for both)
path_g4.previous: G3: the bottom scored against one point, the grip's rest, ((z - rest) / 2)^2: one mirrored valley could not sit at two rests 20 mm apart, so trial 3 scored 49.52, the worst of the four
path_g4.overlap_note: The thumb's and the pinky's paths overlap from z 23.8 to 28.8 for the mean hand (5.0 mm); for the 95th percentile hand by 16.8 mm; for hands shorter than 186 mm (about the 24th percentile, ANSUR II men, normal) they do not overlap: the 5th percentile hand's are 3.5 mm apart, so no mirrored valley lies on both
path_g4.reach: the palm-on-the-hump grip's own failure, a term now (G3 only wrote it on the slides): the index and middle tips past the grooves' front end (z 48, the last section measured), ((mm past) / 2)^2 each; mean hand z 54.8 and 60.6 (the middle past the nose): 51.57
fixes: the felt rule weighted to hold (25, G3 1): at G3's weight the pull toward the start left trial 3's mirrored waist at R 352, 0.5 % gentler than felt (a 3.42 deg turn over the slide)

stay: the outline's mean square distance from the Sora's, 0.1 per mm^2 a side: moving the mirrored waist forward dragged the rear corner in by 2.4 mm through the long arcs' closure, a move no rule asked for (DEV_BOUND only capped it at 2.5)
the mirrored side's pull toward the start counted once (G3 counted it twice when re-packing the lowest point; the reported loss was right, its terms were not)
path_g4.symmetry: a rule, not a term: the result is the lowest loss among the mirrored trials (export_deck.py); trials 2 and 4 stay on the Trials slide, marked lopsided
path_g4.unchanged: the felt rule (each waist turns >= 3.44 deg over the slide, R <= slide / 0.060), the cover rule, the normal-mouse bounds, one minimum per finger, the grooves, the ring finger, true scale, the start (each waist's narrowest point at the grip's rest; mirrored, between the two), Adam, 500 steps, the lowest point kept

trials_g4_on_the_path.result: lifted_sym (trial 3): the lowest loss among the mirrored trials

thumb_g5.decision: Brock 2026-11-08 07:21: "actually no, the thumb never goes that far forward, that's unnatural" (on trial 3's waist at z 23.7, where the G4 slides overlapped; he had liked z 14)
thumb_g5.previous: G1 (trials.place): the thumb tip level with the index's DIP joint (the code took joint [2], the DIP; the comment and G3 called it the middle joint / PIP); an estimate with no source. Mean hand: z 23.8 at the grip, 44.8 with the palm on the hump, 49 mm ahead of the index knuckle
thumb_g5.rule: the thumb from its base: its CMC rides with the hand, 0.275 hand lengths behind the index MCP along the metacarpal line (Veeger 1997 via Goislard de Monsabert 2018) and 10 mm under it (estimate: half way to the palm skin); relaxed (Lee & Jung: MCP 39, IP 10 deg) its bones span 96.0 mm (metacarpal 46.9 = the middle proximal phalanx, Haeri 2022 + Buryanov; phalanges 33.1 and 23.4, Freivalds); in the zero-g grip the span reaches down to the side's contact band (y 15, the middle of G1's 12 to 18) and that sets its reach along the mouse, 74.7 mm; it keeps that reach as the hand moves (it rides with its base and flexes to stay on the side, rather than shooting forward)
thumb_g5.label: derived (sourced inputs; the CMC depth and the contact height are estimates)
thumb_g5.pinky: unchanged (G3): its tip is its own finger's chain, not an estimate; z 28.8 -> 3.9, 24.9 mm (14.7 to 38.4)

cross_checks.clamp_in_place_thumb_mm: p5 14.1, p50 17.5, p95 21.1 (slide_checks.py with the new rule: the base moves back when the palm clamps down with the tips held)
cross_checks.designer: Brock: the thumb sits well behind z 24 (G5 grip z -3.8, landing z 12.9: both behind it)

thumb_g5.no_direct_source: searched for pressure-mapping / contact-location studies of the thumb on a computer mouse and claw-grip kinematics: no peer-reviewed figure found (only vendor blogs); the placement is derived from hand anthropometry

trials_g5_thumb_from_base.result: lifted_sym (trial 3): still the lowest loss among the mirrored trials; its mirrored waist bottom z 3.9 (the rear end of the overlap of the two slides, z 3.9 to 12.9)

joints_at_rest_g6.rule: every joint of the rest pose with its source: orbit where NASA measured it (STS-57: wrist bend 0, wrist side 0, each finger 41 deg mean as one number, its joint not stated), per joint from Lee & Jung on the ground (forearm neutral); the thumb CMC's reference segment not stated in the article; the spread between fingers unsourced (an estimate in the render)

spread.source: none; the render fans the fingers by an estimate (hand3d.X_MCP, X_TIP)

hand_render_g6.what: the hand on gd_rest and gd_joints: the ANSUR II mean hand sculpted as signed distances (tapered fingers, knuckles, pads, nails, creases, thenar and hypothenar eminences, the first web), posed joint by joint from hand.py (each finger's (z, y) joints exactly the model's chain; x fanned by an estimate), meshed by marching cubes (0.55 mm), rendered in Cycles (grey clay, soft studio light, orthographic side view from the thumb's side, mirrored so the nose is on the right, 7 px/mm); deck/tools/gd/hand3d.py, render_hand.py, pack_hand.py
hand_render_g6.frames: 13 relaxing (k 0 to 1), palm on the hump, palm lifted (trial 3), and two between each grip, each as a near layer (index, thumb) and a far layer (the whole hand) that the slide clips by the Sora's profile, so the far fingers pass behind the mouse
hand_render_g6.thumb_in_the_grips: its pad on the side's contact band at G5's z (y 15; x the result's waist, 29.7 mm), facing the wall, solved from its CMC (hand3d.thumb_to): the flexion eases to fit (palm lifted: MCP about 20 deg, IP about 0; palm on the hump: about 56 and 20). The model (G5) stays: its span and reach are unchanged
hand_render_g6.estimates: finger breadths (index 22.6 at the base to 13.2 at the tip), depth 0.9 of breadth, the knuckles' x (index 28, middle 8, ring -11.5, little -29.5 mm; 88 mm across the skin), the tips' x (index 16 and middle -16 as trials.place; ring -31, little -39), the CMC's x (29 mm), the pad's depth (7.4 mm), the free thumb's direction (its metacarpal 45 deg off the index's, reading Lee & Jung's CMC 45 against the index metacarpal; split evenly palmar and radial, 32.8 deg each)
hand_render_g6.model_contact_note: the model lands each finger's bone end on the button (the index 4.9 mm above, the middle 4.9 below, their mean on it); with skin, the index pad rests about on the button and the middle pad lies behind the crown in side view, where the mouse hides it
